properties.statement: Hidden units in a layer can be permuted (with weights adjusted) without changing the network function; the loss landscape has permutation symmetry.
properties.verbatim_quote: One can swap any two units of a hidden layer in a network and – assuming weights are adjusted accordingly – the functionality of the network will remain unchanged.
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.04836 (Ainsworth et al., Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries)
Entezari et al. 2021 (linear mode connectivity conjecture modulo permutation)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.02911 (weight-space symmetry gives permutation saddles connected by equal-loss valleys)

properties.statement: Each continuous differentiable symmetry of an NN architecture yields a conserved quantity under gradient flow (Noether-style); finite learning rate breaks it.
properties.verbatim_quote: any such symmetry imposes stringent geometric constraints on gradients and Hessians, leading to an associated conservation law in the continuous-time limit of stochastic gradient descent (SGD), akin to Noether's theorem in physics
properties.verbatim_quote_2: finite learning rates used in practice can actually break these symmetry-induced conservation laws
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04728 (Kunin, Sagastuy-Brena, Ganguli, Yamins, Tanaka, Neural Mechanics: Symmetry and Broken Conservation Laws in Deep Learning Dynamics)

properties.statement: ReLU positive homogeneity: scaling a unit's incoming weights by c>0 and outgoing weights by 1/c leaves the function unchanged (continuous rescaling symmetry).
properties.verbatim_quote: if the incoming weights of a hidden node with ReLU activation are multiplied by a positive constant c and the outgoing weights are divided by c, the neural network with the new weights will generate exactly the same output as the old one for an arbitrary input
sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.02617 (Neyshabur et al., Path-SGD: Path-Normalized Optimization)
Dinh et al. 2017 (Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets)
